- If sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is rising, model often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day mean by 1–3% when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — adjust downward by 1–2% for 10–15 day horizon.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.7 to -0.5), model lags in reversal — delay peak forecast by 1–2 days and reduce slope.
- If last 3–5 sentiment values are positive, model tends to overpredict 30d high — cap forecast at 1–2% below true 30d max.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is negative and price is trending up — add 2–5% to forecast if sentiment < -0.3 and price > 72.0.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by > 2% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is positive and model forecast is below 72.0, increase forecast by 1–2% to align with sentiment momentum.
